blocking: "South Asian" is claimed everywhere (title, hero line, statement, form) but only Muslim South Asian rituals exist: nikah, walima, mehndi, sangeet, baraat. Hindu and Sikh families (haldi, pheras under the mandap, Anand Karaj) find nothing and no Hindi/Punjabi reply option. Narrow the claim or add the rituals before launch.

The hero loop shows Rome (St Peter's dome is visible in index-desktop-0). Bay Area Persian and Afghan parents will recognise it as a stock Italian wedding, which undercuts the 'we know your families' pitch.

fixes.what: Either (a) add a Hindu/Sikh panel ('Haldi, Pheras & Anand Karaj') to the celebrations and weddings page, add checkboxes 'Haldi', 'Pheras / Mandap', 'Anand Karaj', and add 'Hindi' and 'Punjabi' to the Reply-in select; or (b) change every 'South Asian' to 'Pakistani and Afghan' and keep the current rituals.
fixes.why: The site promises a breadth it does not deliver; a Gujarati or Punjabi mother sees no sign her wedding is understood.

fixes.what: Replace the loop with footage that has no identifiable foreign landmark (a Bay Area estate, a sofreh being set, hands with henna, candle-lit tables), or crop so the skyline is out of frame.
fixes.why: A Rome skyline reads as stock and breaks the local, family-fluent story in the first second.

fixes.what: Remove the inert فارسی item until the Persian site exists, or render it as 'فارسی · به‌زودی' in stone with the 'coming soon' visible, not only in a title tooltip.
fixes.why: Persian-speaking parents tap it, nothing happens, and the footer meanwhile promises 'Persian and Dari pages'; that looks broken, not pending.

fixes.what: Show the one-line notes on desktop too (two rows of stops, or note under each label at 13px), and rename the first stop from 'پرسش' to 'درخواست'.
fixes.why: On desktop a parent sees bare words like 'Bale-boroon / Shirini-khori' and 'Thank-you' with no explanation; پرسش means 'question', not an enquiry.

fixes.where: index.html Sofreh Aghd accordion body and #how-teaser 'Run the day' card
fixes.what: Define the jargon on first use: 'the sofreh key (a one-page guide naming each item on the spread, in both scripts)' and then use 'key' freely after.
fixes.why: 'Checked against the key' appears five times across the site and no family will know what the key is.

fixes.what: Relabel 'Wedding date' as 'First wedding date (or season)' and add an optional select 'Which days' (Engagement, Mehndi/Henna, Aghd/Nikah, Reception/Walima, Not sure yet) plus an optional 'Budget range' select.
fixes.why: These are multi-day weddings; a single date field and no budget question make the first reply slower and the form feel generic to parents who expect to be asked.
